title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the PRC (Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (Trial)

Fa (Jing) Fa [1991] No. 35

For the purpose of correctly implementing the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (Trial) (hereinafter referred to as the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law) and in accordance with the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law and the experience of trial practice, the following opinions are hereby put forward on several issues in bankruptcy proceedings:

I. Jurisdiction

1. An enterprise bankruptcy case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the debtor is located. The place where the debtor is located refers to the place where the main administrative office of the enterprise is located.

2. The basic people's court generally has jurisdiction over bankruptcy cases of enterprises approved and registered by the administrative authorities for industry and commerce at the county, county-level city, or district level.

The intermediate people's court generally has jurisdiction over bankruptcy cases of enterprises approved and registered by the administrative authorities for industry and commerce at the prefecture, prefecture-level city (including the prefecture-level city level) or above.

The level jurisdiction of individual cases may be handled in accordance with the provisions of Article 39, paragraph 1 and paragraph 2, of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law).

II. Bankruptcy Application

3. An application for bankruptcy shall be made in writing.

4. A creditor filing an application for bankruptcy shall provide the following materials to the people's court:

(1) The facts concerning the occurrence of the creditor's rights and relevant evidence;
(2) The nature and amount of the creditor's rights;
(3) Whether the creditor's rights are secured by property; if secured by property, evidence shall be provided;
(4) Relevant evidence that the debtor is unable to pay off its debts when due.

5. A debtor filing an application for bankruptcy shall provide the following materials to the people's court:

(1) A statement explaining the enterprise's loss-making situation;
(2) Accounting statements;
(3) A detailed statement of the enterprise's property conditions and the location of tangible property;
(4) A register of claims and a register of debts (including the names of creditors and debtors, addresses, deposit banks, the time of occurrence of claims and debts, the amounts of claims and debts, whether there is any dispute, etc.);
(5) The consent opinion of the superior competent authority of the bankrupt enterprise or the department authorized by the government regarding the enterprise's application for bankruptcy;
(6) Other materials that the people's court deems should be provided in accordance with the law.

III. Acceptance of Bankruptcy Cases

6. After receiving an application for bankruptcy, the people's court shall review it in accordance with Articles 7, 8, and 3 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, and shall decide within seven days whether to file the case.

If, upon review, the people's court considers that the bankruptcy application requires correction or supplementation of materials, it may order the applicant to make corrections or supplements within a specified period. If corrections or supplements are made within the specified period, the people's court shall decide within seven days from the day after receiving the corrected or supplemented materials whether to file the case; if corrections or supplements are not made within the specified period, the application shall be deemed withdrawn.

7. If an applicant refuses to accept a ruling of the people's court dismissing the bankruptcy application, the applicant has the right to appeal to the people's court at the next higher level. The time limit for appeal is ten days.

8. The term "unable to pay off debts when due" as used in Article 3, paragraph 1, of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law refers to:

(1) The time limit for payment of the debt has already expired;
(2) The creditor has already demanded payment;
(3) The debtor is clearly lacking the ability to pay.

If the debtor has stopped paying due debts and such state is continuous, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, it may be presumed to be "unable to pay off debts when due."

9. After accepting a bankruptcy case, the people's court shall form a collegial panel for trial.

10. After accepting a bankruptcy case, the people's court shall issue a public notice within ten days. In addition to posting the notice on the bulletin board of the people's court that accepted the bankruptcy case, the notice shall also be published in local or national newspapers or periodicals depending on the specific circumstances of the case (such as the areas where creditors are distributed, the location of the bankruptcy property, etc.). The public notice shall include the following contents:

(1) The date of filing the case;
(2) The debtor in the bankruptcy case;
(3) The time limit and place for declaring claims, and the legal consequences of failing to declare within the time limit;
(4) The date and place of the first creditors' meeting, etc.

11. After accepting a bankruptcy case, the people's court shall notify the debtor within ten days, and within ten days after receiving the register of debts submitted by the debtor, shall notify known creditors.

The notice to known creditors shall include the contents specified in items (3) and (4) of Article 10 of these Opinions.

12. After accepting a bankruptcy case, other economic dispute cases in which the bankrupt enterprise is the debtor shall be handled separately according to the following different circumstances:

(1) If the case has already been adjudicated but not yet executed, execution shall be suspended, and the creditor shall declare its claim to the people's court that accepted the bankruptcy case on the basis of the effective legal instrument;
(2) If the case has not yet been adjudicated and there is no other person with joint and several liability, the action shall be terminated, and the creditor shall declare its claim to the people's court that accepted the bankruptcy case;
(3) If the case has not yet been adjudicated and there is another person with joint and several liability, the action shall be suspended, and the creditor shall declare its claim to the people's court that accepted the bankruptcy case. After the bankruptcy proceedings are concluded, the trial shall be resumed.

13. After accepting a bankruptcy case, if there are other economic dispute cases in which the bankrupt enterprise is the creditor and the people's court hearing the case cannot conclude the case within three months, it shall transfer the case to the people's court that accepted the bankruptcy case, which shall handle it in accordance with Articles 45 and 46 of these Opinions.

14. After accepting a bankruptcy case, if the people's court finds that a case in which the bankrupt enterprise is the creditor is pending in another people's court and is difficult to conclude within three months, it shall notify that people's court to transfer the case.

15. During civil proceedings or civil execution proceedings, if the people's court learns that the debtor is unable to pay off its debts when due, it shall inform the debtor that it may apply for bankruptcy to the people's court at its location.

If the debtor applies for bankruptcy, the people's court at the debtor's location shall declare the debtor bankrupt in accordance with the law.

If the debtor does not apply for bankruptcy, the court shall not declare the debtor bankrupt ex officio. The original proceedings or execution proceedings may continue.

16. In accordance with the provisions of Article 10, paragraph 2, of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, if the debtor acts as a surety for another entity, it shall, within five days after receiving the notice of acceptance of the bankruptcy case from the people's court, inform the relevant parties. After learning of the bankruptcy of the surety (debtor), the creditor has the option to decide whether to include its claim as a bankruptcy claim. If the creditor neither participates in the bankruptcy proceedings nor informs the surety, the surety's (debtor's) guarantee obligation shall terminate from that moment; if the creditor participates in the bankruptcy proceedings, the amount of the creditor's claim at the time of the bankruptcy declaration shall constitute the bankruptcy claim, and after participating in the distribution, the creditor may still seek recourse from the principal debtor for the portion of the claim not satisfied.

17. After the people's court issues a notice of case filing, creditors may only declare claims and may not initiate new lawsuits against the people's court that accepted the bankruptcy case. The declaration shall contain the first three items listed in Article 4 of these Opinions.

18. The people's court shall assign special personnel to register and compile a ledger for the declared claims.

19. After accepting a bankruptcy case, the people's court shall immediately notify the debtor to stop repaying debts from the date of receipt of the notice. Any payments necessary for the normal production and operation of the debtor shall, before the establishment of the liquidation committee, be subject to the review and approval of the people's court.

If, after receiving the notice from the people's court to stop repaying debts, the debtor still repays debts to some creditors or commits any of the acts listed in Article 35, paragraph 1, of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the people's court shall rule such acts invalid, recover the property, and may, in accordance with Articles 102 and 104 of the Civil Procedure Law, impose sanctions on the legal representative, the person in charge of the superior competent authority, and other directly responsible persons.

20. After accepting a bankruptcy case, the people's court shall promptly notify the debtor's depository bank to stop handling settlement business for the debtor's debt repayment; any payment by the depository bank for expenses necessary to maintain the debtor's normal production and operation shall require the permission of the people's court.

21. After receiving the notice from the people's court, the debtor's depository bank shall not deduct the debtor's existing deposits or incoming remittances to offset loans. Any such deduction shall be invalid, and the deducted amount shall be returned. If the bank refuses to return the amount, the people's court shall rule that it must be returned and shall issue a notice of assistance in execution to the depository bank, and may, in accordance with Articles 102 and 104 of the Civil Procedure Law, impose sanctions on the relevant personnel and directly responsible persons.

22. After accepting a bankruptcy case, the people's court shall issue a public notice to all employees of the enterprise, requiring them to protect the enterprise's property and not to unlawfully handle the enterprise's account books, documents, materials, or seals, and not to conceal, distribute without authorization, transfer without compensation, or sell the enterprise's property at an abnormally low price.

If, before the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings, the legal representative of the bankrupt enterprise abandons his or her post without authorization, evades in other ways, refuses to handle the handover procedures with the liquidation committee, or commits any of the acts listed in Article 102 of the Civil Procedure Law, the people's court may, depending on the gravity of the circumstances, impose a fine or detention; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.

IV. Creditors' Meeting

23. The first creditors' meeting shall be presided over by the people's court, and subsequent meetings shall be presided over by the chairman of the meeting.

24. When convening the first creditors' meeting, the people's court shall announce the results of the examination of creditors' qualifications, designate and announce the chairman of the creditors' meeting, announce the functions of the creditors' meeting and other relevant matters, and report on the basic situation of the debtor's production, operation, property, and debts.

25. When the chairman of the creditors' meeting convenes a creditors' meeting, he or she shall report to the people's court three days before sending out the notice.

26. A creditor may entrust an agent to attend the creditors' meeting and exercise the right to vote. The agent shall submit a power of attorney signed and sealed by the principal to the people's court or the chairman of the creditors' meeting.

27. When convening a creditors' meeting, the convener shall notify the creditors of the time, place, content, and purpose of the meeting seven days (twenty days for those outside the locality) before the meeting.

28. The voting on resolutions of the creditors' meeting shall count the votes based on the creditors attending the meeting who have the right to vote, and calculate the amount of creditor's rights voted based on the creditor's rights they represent.

29. The terms "more than half" and "two-thirds or more" in Article 16, paragraph 1, of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law include the figure itself; "more than half" does not include the figure itself.

30. The amount of creditor's rights represented by creditors exercising the right to vote shall be calculated based on the amount of creditor's rights determined by the creditors' meeting. If there is a dispute over the amount of creditor's rights determined by the creditors' meeting, the people's court shall review and rule on the matter, and the amount shall be calculated based on the creditor's rights confirmed by the ruling.

31. If the liquidation committee proposes a plan for the distribution of bankruptcy property and the plan is not adopted after multiple discussions by the creditors' meeting, the people's court shall promptly make a ruling based on the specific circumstances of the case.

32. The superior competent authority of the debtor may send representatives to attend the creditors' meeting as non-voting participants. The legal representative of the debtor must attend the creditors' meeting and is obliged to answer questions from creditors; if he or she refuses to attend, the people's court may, in accordance with Article 100 of the Civil Procedure Law, issue a warrant for compulsory appearance.

V. Composition and Rehabilitation

33. If an enterprise is applied for bankruptcy by creditors and its superior competent authority applies for rehabilitation of the enterprise, it shall submit a rehabilitation plan to the people's court and the creditors' meeting. The rehabilitation plan shall contain the following contents:

(1) An analysis of the reasons why the enterprise has reached the brink of bankruptcy;
(2) A plan for adjusting or establishing a new leadership team for the enterprise;
(3) Measures for improving operational management and the feasibility of measures for transformation and product conversion;
(4) Methods for turning losses into profits;
(5) The time limit for rehabilitation (not exceeding two years) and the objectives, etc.

34. The enterprise for which rehabilitation is applied shall submit a draft composition agreement to the creditors' meeting. The draft composition agreement shall contain the following contents:

(1) The sources of property for repaying debts;
(2) The method for repaying debts;
(3) The time limit for repaying debts, etc.

If the enterprise for which rehabilitation is applied requests a reduction in the amount of debts, it shall also specify the amount requested to be reduced.

35. If the enterprise and the creditors' meeting reach a composition agreement, and after the people's court approves it, the people's court shall issue a public notice to suspend the bankruptcy proceedings; if the enterprise and the creditors fail to reach a composition agreement, the people's court shall rule to declare the enterprise bankrupt.

36. During the rehabilitation period of the enterprise, the superior competent authority of the enterprise shall periodically report to the creditors' meeting and the people's court on the status of the rehabilitation and the implementation of the composition agreement.

37. During the rehabilitation period of the enterprise, if the enterprise falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 21, items (1) and (3), of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, some creditors or the creditors' meeting have the right to apply for the termination of the rehabilitation.

38. During the rehabilitation period of the enterprise, if the people's court discovers that the debtor falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 21 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, it shall rule to terminate the rehabilitation of the enterprise and declare it bankrupt.

39. After rehabilitation, if the enterprise is able to repay its due debts, it shall only repay them in accordance with the time limit and amount specified in the composition agreement. However, this does not apply to claims secured by property where the priority right has not been waived.

After the acceptance of the bankruptcy case but before the declaration of bankruptcy, a holder of a security interest may not exercise the priority right without the consent of the people's court.

40. After accepting a bankruptcy case, if the superior competent authority of the enterprise does not apply for rehabilitation, the people's court may declare the enterprise bankrupt in accordance with the law.

VI. Bankruptcy Declaration

41. The declaration of bankruptcy of an enterprise by the people's court shall be conducted publicly.

42. When the people's court declares an enterprise bankrupt, it shall notify the creditors and the debtor to appear in court and announce the ruling in court. Failure to appear in court does not affect the validity of the ruling.

43. The ruling of the people's court declaring an enterprise bankrupt shall take legal effect from the date of the declaration, and the bankrupt enterprise shall cease its production and business activities from that date, unless the people's court or the liquidation committee considers it truly necessary to continue production and operation.

44. When the people's court rules to declare an enterprise bankrupt, it may simultaneously issue a public notice. The public notice shall contain the following contents:

(1) The enterprise's losses and asset-liability situation;
(2) The reasons and legal basis for declaring the enterprise bankrupt;
(3) The date of the declaration of bankruptcy;
(4) The protection of the bankrupt enterprise's property, account books, documents, materials, and seals after the declaration of bankruptcy, etc.

The public notice shall be affixed with the seal of the people's court.

45. After declaring an enterprise bankrupt, the people's court shall notify the debtors or property holders of the bankrupt enterprise to repay debts or deliver property to the liquidation committee.

46. After receiving the above-mentioned notice from the people's court, the debtors or property holders of the bankrupt enterprise shall repay debts or deliver property to the liquidation committee in the amount and within the time limit specified in the notice; if they object to the notified amount of debt or the type or quantity of property, they may, within seven days, request the people's court to rule on the matter; if they neither repay or deliver nor raise an objection within the time limit, the liquidation committee shall apply to the people's court for a ruling and subsequent compulsory execution.

47. After declaring an enterprise bankrupt, the people's court shall notify (with a copy of the ruling declaring the enterprise bankrupt attached) the depository bank of the bankrupt enterprise, specifying that the bank account may only be used by the liquidation committee.

48. After declaring an enterprise bankrupt, the people's court may send copies of the ruling declaring the enterprise bankrupt to the relevant government supervision departments and audit departments.

49. After an enterprise is declared bankrupt, the people's court shall designate necessary personnel to remain at the enterprise. The legal representative of the bankrupt enterprise and the personnel in charge of finance and accounting, statistics, warehousing, and security must remain; other personnel who need to remain and the number of such personnel shall be determined by the liquidation committee.

VII. Bankruptcy Liquidation

50. Before the establishment of the liquidation committee, the people's court shall, in consultation with the people's government at the same level, designate members of the liquidation committee by official letter from among the enterprise's superior competent authority, government finance, administrative authorities for industry and commerce, planning commission, audit, taxation, prices, labor, personnel departments, and professionals. Once designated, the relevant units and personnel shall not make excuses to refuse or leave their posts without authorization. If it is truly impossible to perform duties due to objective circumstances, the people's court may designate another person.

The head of the liquidation committee shall be designated by the people's court.

51. The liquidation committee may appoint a certain number of accountants from an accounting firm and other staff.

52. The liquidation committee is responsible to the people's court and reports its work to it, and accepts the supervision of the people's court. If the liquidation committee engages in acts that harm the interests of creditors or other illegal acts, the people's court shall correct them and may remove incompetent members from the liquidation committee and designate new members.

53. The liquidation committee shall attend the creditors' meeting as a non-voting participant and accept the supervision of the creditors' meeting. If a decision of the liquidation committee is contrary to the interests of the creditors, the creditors may apply to the people's court for a ruling to revoke it.

54. After the declaration of bankruptcy, the original legal representative of the bankrupt enterprise shall organize the enterprise's financial and accounting personnel to prepare the final financial accounts, the warehousing personnel to prepare a property inventory, and the business personnel to settle outstanding business transactions such as purchases and sales. When the liquidation committee takes over the bankrupt enterprise, the original legal representative of the bankrupt enterprise shall handle the handover to the liquidation committee.

55. If the liquidation committee decides to rescind a contract and the other party suffers damages due to the rescission, any dispute over damages shall be resolved by a ruling of the people's court. The amount of damages determined in the ruling shall be included in the bankruptcy claims.

56. After taking over the bankrupt enterprise, the liquidation committee shall organize the personnel remaining at the enterprise and the staff of the liquidation committee to count, register, and compile a ledger of all property of the bankrupt enterprise, and ascertain the total amount of the enterprise's actual property.

57. The liquidation committee shall revalue the bankruptcy property; for fixed assets that have been fully depreciated, their residual value shall be revalued; for defective or deteriorated property, a conversion value shall be calculated; for property that does not need to be converted, it shall be valued at its original value.

58. The liquidation committee shall distribute the property of the bankrupt enterprise, with cash distribution as the principle; distribution in kind may also be adopted, or a combination of both methods; if the claims of the bankrupt enterprise have not been recovered at the time of distribution, such claims may also be distributed proportionally to the creditors of the bankrupt enterprise, and the debtors of the bankrupt enterprise shall be notified at the same time.

59. When the liquidation committee disposes of the property of the bankrupt enterprise, it may, after reasonably pricing the property in kind, distribute it to the creditors, or it may sell it by conversion into cash. Sales shall be conducted publicly, such as by public auction. If the bankruptcy property is subject to restricted transfer, it shall be purchased by the department designated by the state.

60. If the bankrupt enterprise has formed a partnership-type or corporate-type joint venture with others, the property invested by the bankrupt enterprise as a capital contribution and the income due shall be recovered; if recovery is not possible, the property may be transferred, and the other party to the joint venture has a preemptive right to purchase under equal conditions. If the bankrupt enterprise is a party to a partnership-type joint venture, it shall bear joint and several liability for all debts of the joint venture before its withdrawal, and the creditors of the joint venture may participate in the bankruptcy proceedings as creditors. If the liquidation committee's recovery of the property invested by the bankrupt enterprise and the income due causes damage to the other party to the joint venture, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 55 of these Opinions.

61. In accordance with Article 89 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 13, paragraph 1, of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, if, before the principal debtor is declared bankrupt, the surety has paid the debt on behalf of the principal debtor, the surety has the right to declare the amount paid as a bankruptcy claim to the people's court and participate in the distribution; if, before the principal debtor is declared bankrupt, the surety has not paid the debt on behalf of the principal debtor, the matter shall be handled in the following two situations:

(1) The creditor may participate in the bankruptcy proceedings as a bankruptcy creditor, declare the full amount of its claim as a bankruptcy claim and participate in the distribution, and may also seek recourse from the surety for the portion not satisfied;
(2) If the surety learns before the expiration of the time limit for declaring claims that the creditor will not participate in the bankruptcy proceedings, the surety may declare the amount of the guaranteed debt as a bankruptcy claim and participate in the distribution.

62. Where the drawer or endorser of a negotiable instrument (bill of exchange, promissory note, or cheque) is declared bankrupt, and the payer or acceptor makes payment or acceptance without knowledge of such fact, the creditor's rights arising therefrom shall be bankruptcy claims, and the payer or acceptor shall be the creditor.

63. Where the proceeds from the mortgaged property or other security property of the bankrupt enterprise are insufficient to cover the amount of the secured debt, the shortfall shall be included in the bankruptcy claims.

64. Interest-bearing bankruptcy claims shall be calculated up to the date of the declaration of bankruptcy.

65. Where a claim of the bankrupt enterprise has not yet fallen due at the time of the declaration of bankruptcy, it shall be included in the bankruptcy property as a due claim, provided that the interest not yet accrued and other losses shall be deducted. Property of the bankrupt enterprise that is truly irrecoverable shall not be included in the bankruptcy property for distribution.

66. The term "expenses" in Article 34, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law includes the wages and labor insurance expenses of the retained staff of the bankrupt enterprise, as well as the necessary expenses of the liquidation committee.

67. The liquidation committee shall, based on the results of liquidation, prepare a detailed inventory of the bankruptcy property and a balance sheet, and shall propose a plan for the distribution of the bankruptcy property.

68. After the distribution plan for the bankruptcy property has been discussed and adopted by the creditors' meeting and confirmed by a ruling of the people's court, the liquidation committee shall promptly notify the creditors to collect their property within a specified time limit. If the property is not collected within the specified time limit, it may be placed in deposit.

69. When collecting property, a creditor shall produce a certificate indicating the creditor's specific address and bank account number.

70. After the distribution of the bankruptcy property is completed, and the liquidation committee has requested the people's court to conclude the bankruptcy proceedings, the people's court shall, within seven days, render a ruling concluding the bankruptcy proceedings.

71. After the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings, the liquidation committee shall handle the cancellation of the registration of the bankrupt enterprise with the original registration authority of the bankrupt enterprise, and shall promptly inform the people's court of the handling status.

72. After the cancellation of the registration of the bankrupt enterprise, the people's court shall announce the dissolution of the liquidation committee.

73. The right to claim property of the bankrupt enterprise discovered after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings shall be exercised by the higher-level supervising authority of the bankrupt enterprise. The property recovered shall be distributed by the people's court in accordance with Article 37 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law. If the property is relatively small and the people's court considers further distribution unnecessary, it may be allocated to the higher-level supervising authority of the bankrupt enterprise.

VIII. Miscellaneous

74. The bankruptcy and debt repayment procedures for legal persons of non-enterprise-owned enterprises shall be governed by the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law.

75. With the exception of the ruling rejecting the bankruptcy petition, all rulings made by the people's court in bankruptcy cases shall not be subject to appeal. If a party disagrees with a ruling, it may apply to the original people's court that made the ruling for reconsideration. However, the enforcement of the ruling shall not be suspended during the reconsideration period.

76. If a debtor or property holder of the bankrupt enterprise objects to the amount of debt or the quantity of property specified in the notice from the people's court for payment or delivery, and such objection is rejected upon examination by the people's court, the case acceptance fee shall be paid in accordance with the standard specified in Article 5, paragraph (4) of the Measures for the Collection of Litigation Fees by the People's Courts.

November 7, 1991
